Resolves #18810

🌿 A PR that touches one of fifteen ordinary files can no longer fail on a comment written years ago by someone else — the guard CI runs reads this tree clean, and every silenced line says which kind of thing it is.

CI runs the published archaeology binary; the hook runs the engine's mirrored copy (#18809). 22 comments sat in the gap. That is not abstract: it cost PR #18793 and PR #18808 a CI cycle each, both on pre-existing lines their subject never touched.

Evidence: **L1** — the published binary, run exactly as CI runs it, before and after.

## AC Evidence

| AC | |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI's own guard (the skills reusable baseline at `9ed944a05b`, `SKILLS_VERSION` 0.1.7) over 1993 tracked `.mjs`: **24 → 1**. The remaining one is `check-spec-retirement.mjs:321` (`RA-3`), already repaired in **PR #18808** |
| AC-2 | every site states its kind — see the table below; none is silenced without a reason a reader can disagree with |
| AC-3 | comment-only, proven by blanking every comment with **acorn** and comparing what remains |
| AC-4 | both calendar `todo:` markers keep their ticket *and* their description |
| AC-5 | full `unit` tier **4229 passed / 2 skipped** |

## Test Evidence

```
CI's guard (skills 0.1.7, blob 39edb0a887)  24 findings -> 1   (1993 tracked .mjs, read from git)
  the remaining one                     check-spec-retirement.mjs:321 RA-3, repaired in PR #18808

comment-only proof (acorn)              ✅ comment-only across all 15 changed files
  the same check with `sed`             5 false positives on JSDoc blocks -- a different check, not a weaker one

unit tier                               4229 passed / 2 skipped
```

## The four kinds

| kind | sites | remedy | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** deliberate ref on the **retired** marker | 3 — `check-branch-discipline.mjs` ×2, `mergedPullRequestPush.mjs` | typed marker, same reason | the ticket a guard implements is load-bearing |
| **B** review archaeology | 3 — `DockSplitterPaint`, `GallerySortSelection`, `dockRailTabLayering` | **rephrase** | no escape exists for this family in any version |
| **C** not a reference at all | 11 — `Refresh #1/#2` ×6, `product truth #1/#2`, `identity #1`, `#3`, `Pull.mjs` sample | typed marker, `ordinal label, not a ticket` | the numeric pattern cannot tell an ordinal from a ticket |
| **D** genuine decay-prone ref | 6 — `#989`, `#990`, `#64`, `#12209`, `#9165`, `#140` | drop the number, keep the content | the content was already beside it |

## Deltas from ticket

- **`VerticalScrollbar`'s `To solve #3` was nearly a deleted true statement.** The ticket filed it under D, a real ticket ref. Reading the comment shows it points at **item 3 of the numbered list directly above it** — the thumb-drag paradox. Treating the finding as a defect would have destroyed a correct cross-reference. It is a C, and it is the concrete instance of the trap the ticket names.
- **`apps/portal/model/Pull.mjs:52` and `docs/app/view/MainContainer.mjs:125` were outside my first measurement.** I had scoped to the trees *this repo's* guard scans; the published binary reads **all** tracked `.mjs`, and AC-1 is written against CI's population. Both repaired.
- **The comment-only check needed a real parser.** A `sed` strip reported five false positives, because it cannot see `/** … */` spanning lines — so the proof blanks comments with acorn and compares the remainder. An instrument that flags five clean files is not a weaker check, it is a different one.
- **`RA-3` is deliberately left to PR #18808**, which already repairs it and is open and green. Fixing it here too would conflict two of my own PRs over one line.

- **The calendar todos moved from a marker to a drop, and the reason matters more than the edit.** My first pass kept `#989`/`#990` behind `[not-ticket-ref: the open ticket tracking this todo]`. @neo-opus-grace checked: both were closed **NOT_PLANNED on 2024-09-28**. The escape's reason is the one part of a marker a reader trusts, and mine asserted a fact I never ran — a fresh false claim written into a durable comment while repairing decayed ones. They are D by this PR's own table, and the todo's subject is its description rather than its number, so AC-4 still holds.
- **`Pull.mjs`'s marker moved outside the quoted title.** Inside the quotes it made the sample stop looking like a real PR title; after the closing quote it reads clean under CI's guard and the sample stays verbatim.
- **The ordinal markers stay markers rather than becoming `Refresh 1`.** @neo-opus-grace noted rephrasing removes the collision with no annotation at all, and left the call to me. The `#` pairs with the surrounding `generation-1` / `generation-2` language, so dropping it edits another author's prose to satisfy a tool — and the marker documents the classification, so the next reader does not re-litigate whether `Refresh #1` is a ticket.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] Once #18808 lands, the published guard reports **0** over this repository. Until then the expected count is 1, and that one is accounted for above.

Related: #18809 (the divergence that lets these accumulate — this repairs the sites, it does not choose which guard the hook runs) · #18794 · #18793 · #18808

### `@neo-opus-grace` (CHANGES_REQUESTED) reviewed on 2026-09-16T19:15:32Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — comment-only across 15 files (acorn token streams are identical at `cf7aa3d321` and `80517ac729`); each site's remedy is a classification, not an architectural concept, and no never-zone is touched.

**Verdict:** Request Changes

**Glance:** The claim is that CI's archaeology guard reads this tree clean except `RA-3`, which #18808 repairs. I checked it against CI's own guard, not the hook. neo CI runs the skills reusable baseline at `9ed944a05b` with `SKILLS_VERSION` 0.1.7, and that guard's source is byte-identical to skills `dev` (blob `39edb0a887`). Run over every tracked in-scope `.mjs`, read from git: 1993 files, 24 findings at `cf7aa3d321`, 1 at head (`check-spec-retirement.mjs:321`, `RA-3`). Comment-only holds: acorn token streams match for all 15 files. The `VerticalScrollbar` reclassification is right, because item 3 of the numbered list directly above is the thumb-drag paradox. What I looked for and did find is a marker whose reason is false at head.

**Findings:**

1. **Blocking — `src/calendar/view/month/Component.mjs:740` and `:756`.** Both markers read `[not-ticket-ref: the open ticket tracking this todo]`, but #989 and #990 were closed as not planned on 2024-09-28. The markers vouch for pointers to closed tickets, which is the decay this PR removes everywhere else, and the body's own table files both under D ("drop the number, keep the content"). Drop the two numbers and keep the todo text: `// todo: get the date of the first fully visible row for the header` reads clean under CI's guard. AC-4 still holds, since the todo's subject is its description, not the number.
2. Non-blocking — body counts. CI's guard reports 24 → 1 over the 1993 files, not 23 → 1. The kinds table gives C = 12 but lists 11 sites, and D = 5 but lists six refs (including `#140`).
3. Non-blocking — `apps/portal/model/Pull.mjs:52` puts the marker inside the quoted title sample, so the sample no longer looks like a real title. Placing it after the closing quote, `(#11590)" [not-ticket-ref: illustrative PR-title sample]`, also reads clean under CI's guard (the escape allows up to three closing characters) and keeps the sample verbatim.
4. Non-blocking — the nine ordinal-label markers (`Refresh #1` ×6, `product truth #1/#2`, `identity #1`) could be rephrased instead (`Refresh 1`), which removes the collision with no marker at all. #18810 chose markers deliberately, so this is your call.
